answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy makes every identity earn its standing through a long voyage of attested work: a new agent starts with zero reputation and must complete many small verified tasks before it can claim meaningful rewards, like a single marble earning its place in a mosaic one piece at a time. Attackers face a real cost, since each fake identity must repeat the whole voyage, while the nectar, the actual reward, only flows to identities with a proven history, so spinning up thousands of empty shells buys nothing.
